properties.title: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued October 19 at 4:56PM MDT until October 19 at 5:45PM MDT by NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM
properties.description:
SVREPZ

The National Weather Service in El Paso has issued a

* Severe Thunderstorm Warning for...
South central Grant County in southwestern New Mexico...
West central Luna County in southwestern New Mexico...

* Until 545 PM MDT.

* At 456 PM MDT, a severe thunderstorm was located 10 miles west of
Gage, moving east at 25 mph.

HAZARD...Two inch hail and 60 mph wind gusts.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...People and animals outdoors will be injured. Expect hail
damage to roofs, siding, windows, and vehicles. Expect
wind damage to roofs, siding, and trees.

* Locations impacted include...
Gage.

This includes Interstate 10 in New Mexico between mile markers 48 and
72.
properties.instruction:
Remain alert for a possible tornado! Tornadoes can develop quickly
from severe thunderstorms. If you spot a tornado go at once into the
basement or small central room in a sturdy structure.

For your protection move to an interior room on the lowest floor of a
building.
properties.sender: NWS El Paso Tx/Santa Teresa NM

properties.title: Severe Thunderstorm Warning issued October 19 at 3:50PM MST until October 19 at 4:15PM MST by NWS Tucson AZ
properties.description:
At 350 PM MST, a severe thunderstorm was located 11 miles north of
Bowie, moving east at 25 mph.

HAZARD...60 mph wind gusts and quarter size hail.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Hail damage to vehicles is expected. Expect wind damage to
roofs, siding, and trees.

Locations impacted include...
Mainly rural areas of North Central Cochise and Southeastern Graham
Counties.

This includes Interstate 10 near mile marker 357.
properties.instruction:
Seek shelter inside a well-built structure and stay away from
windows. This storm is capable of producing damaging winds and large
hail.

Continuous cloud to ground lightning is occurring with this storm.
Lightning is one of nature's leading killers. Remember, if you can
hear thunder, you are close enough to be struck by lightning.

Report severe weather to your nearest law enforcement agency or the
National Weather Service office in Tucson.

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued October 19 at 6:31PM AST until October 19 at 8:30PM AST by NWS San Juan PR
properties.description:
* WHAT...Urban area and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Dorado in Puerto Rico...
Toa Baja in Puerto Rico...
Vega Alta in Puerto Rico...

* WHEN...Until 830 PM AST.

* IMPACTS...Urban area and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall is expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 629 PM AST, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. This  will cause urban and small stream flooding.
Between 1 and 2.2 inches of rain have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.
properties.area: Dorado, PR; Toa Baja, PR; Vega Alta, PR

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued October 19 at 2:55PM MST until October 19 at 5:00PM MST by NWS Tucson AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Small stream flooding caused by excessive rainfall is
expected.

* WHERE...Northern Cochise County in southeastern Arizona...

* WHEN...Until 500 PM MST.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous flows over low-water crossings. Some low-water
crossings may become impassable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 255 PM MST, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. This will cause small stream flooding. Between 0.5
and 0.8 inches of rain have fallen.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of Northern Cochise County.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued October 19 at 11:54AM AKDT until October 19 at 4:00PM AKDT by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Anchorage and Eagle River

* WHEN...Until 400 PM AKDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Storm drains and ditches may become clogged with debris. Ponding of
water on area roadways and low-lying areas is occurring or is
imminent.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 1149 AM AKDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges
indicated heavy rain across the advisory area. Between 0.3 and
0.6 inches of rain have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts of
0.1 to 0.3 inches are possible.
- Heavy rain will continue through later this afternoon. Heavy rain
may lead to ponding of water on roadways and low-lying areas. Use
caution and slow down when driving through heavy rain. Water
levels along small waterways are expected to be at or above
bankfull through Wednesday morning.


- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued October 19 at 9:56AM EDT by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

St Johns River Near Astor affecting Lake and Volusia Counties.

.Persistent northeast winds have caused river levels on the St Johns
at Astor to rise into Moderate Flood Stage this morning. The river is
forecast to climb slowly through Moderate Flood Stage through the end
of this week.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 3.0 feet, Water approaches or may enter lowest homes
on or near Wildhog Road and nearby canals. Flooding reaches the
parking lot of the Juno Trail Apartments. Flooding on portions of
Alligator Road and Holiday Road. Lowest lying yards along Blue
Creek are flooded. Roads at Astor Landing Campground and Lake
Dexter Boat Ramp begin to flood. Water enters lower homes closest
to the river on McPherson Lane.

At 3.5 feet, Canals have overflowed into yards. Homes on or near
Wildhog and Bonnet roads become inaccessible with several inches of
water inside homes along the river and canals. Docks at Astor Bridge
marina and throughout Astor are completely submerged. Bartram Rd and
Holiday Circle are inaccessible with yards completely submerged.
Clair Street is inaccessible. Roads flooded in South Moon Fish Camp,
docks and yards at condominiums on Juno Trail and water breaches the
sea wall at Blair's Jungle Den.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:30 AM EDT Monday the stage was 3.0 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 8:30 AM EDT Monday was 3.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to remain steady above flood
stage at 3.1 feet.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 1115 PM EDT.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued October 19 at 9:33AM EDT by NWS Jacksonville FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in southeast
Georgia...

Satilla River At Atkinson affecting Brantley County.

Additional information is available at
https://water.weather.gov/wfo/JAX

The next statement will be issued Tuesday morning at 945 AM EDT.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Satilla River at Atkinson.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 13.0 feet, Warners Landing, Louis Landing and
secondary roads around KOA campgrounds begin to flood. At 14.0
feet, River Rock Road begins to experience flooding across the
road.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:45 AM EDT Monday the stage was 14.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to crest around 14.2 feet this
afternoon, with a slow falling trend the remainder of the week.
- Flood stage is 13.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued October 15 at 8:39AM CDT until October 19 at 7:00PM CDT by NWS Norman OK
properties.description:
...The Flood Advisory continues for the following rivers in Texas...
Oklahoma...

Red River near Burkburnett affecting Wichita, Cotton, Tillman,
Jefferson and Clay Counties.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...Red River near Burkburnett.

* WHEN...Until Monday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 8.0 feet, Near bankfull conditions extend along the
Red River near Davidson... Oklahoma downstream to areas near
Burkburnett and Taylor... Oklahoma.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 AM CDT Thursday the stage was 2.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 9.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 7.7 feet
Saturday evening.
- Action stage is 7.0 feet.
- Flood stage is 9.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued this evening at 845 PM CDT.
